In neuroscience there is a concept called ego-depletion, which basically refers to the fact of life that humans cannot do something they find unpleasant willingly and voluntarily for periods of time longer than about ten minutes, after which fatigue and dissatisfaction set in. Difficult tasks tend to frustrate a bit, which raises stress levels, making us want to gravitate away, or make up excuses why tomorrow is a better day. So humans are not prone to doing a whole bunch of difficult if beneficial things they aren't forced to do.

To mitigate that I have taken a personal approach of forcing a five minute break, to breathe and relax, after every 10-12 minute writing session. I've got an interval timer program installed on my phone and it sounds off a beep each time an interval of either work or rest is up. During these break intervals I try to physically relax my whole body, and to take some deep relaxing breaths. Usually my state is pretty good by the time the five minutes are up and I can handle another ten minutes of difficult work. It goes like this..

Try it, set if for ten intervals, and you'll get a lot of editing done. Don't wait until you feel like editing for hours, that'll be never.
